Explain how a memory-bound decode step differs from a compute-bound one.
anchors.text:
A memory-bound decode step is one where the performance is limited by the speed of accessing memory, whereas a compute-bound step is limited by the processing power of the CPU. In a memory-bound step, the CPU spends more time waiting for data to be fetched from memory, while in a compute-bound step, the CPU is fully utilized performing calculations.
